newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends below T$28 for 1st time since 1989.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends below T$28 for 1st time since 1989.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar sank to its lowest close in more than eight years against the U.S. currency on Tuesday after the central bank abandoned its longtime defence of T$28 to the U.S. dollar, dealers said.

The recently depreciating currency tested below T$28 shortly after the opening and -- as the bank's non-interfence became apparent -- promptly sank to an intra-day low of T$28.20 before recovering mildly to end the day at T$28.170.
The rate marked the exchange rate's lowest level since it traded in the T$28-29 range in 1988.
Turnover through dealers was a voluminous US$543.5 million, the heaviest since it hit US$590.5 million on March 24.
The T$28.170 close represented a 2.4 percent depreciation from the central bank's previous longtime defence of T$27.5.

The bank had defended T$27.5 for some seven years -- even in 1995-96 when communist China menaced rival Taiwan with months of military drills and unarmed ballistic missile tests, sparking a flight to greenbacks, gold and other safe havens.
Just two months after those tensions eased, in May 1996, the central bank publicly dropped its T$27.5 defence -- a move seen widely as an invitation for an export-boosting depreciation.

Dealers said the bank's hands-off policy on Tuesday fuelled selling of the local dollar, which had come under depreciation pressure due to the U.S. dollar's strength overseas as well as speculative attacks through non-delivery forward trading.

"The central bank decision to let go of its defence sparked hectic buying of the U.S. dollar, especially from those who had taken a short position on the greenback," said one dealer from a foreign bank.
"Psychologically it gave investors the feeling that the Taiwan dollar would sink lower," she said.
Dealers said that although the central bank allowed the rate to fall below T$28, it likely would defend the currency again if the depreciation continued unchecked or accelerated.
Longer-range, several dealers said they expected the Taiwan dollar to test T$28.5 or even T$29 before the end of 1997.
A T$28.00-25 range was seen for Wednesday.
